rationales: Mist consists of tiny liquid-water droplets dispersed in a gas, so it is liquid in gas.
Gas in liquid describes a gas dispersed in a liquid, such as soda bubbles.
Solid in gas describes solid particles dispersed in a gas, such as smoke.
Gas in solid describes gas dispersed in a solid, not mist.
Graphite is a soft form of carbon, not extremely hard.
Phosphorus is a non-metal but is not extremely hard.
Iodine is a brittle solid, not extremely hard.
Diamond is an extremely hard form of carbon.
Metals are generally electropositive, not electronegative.
Electron affinity does not explain why metals readily lose electrons.
Metals are electropositive and tend to lose electrons to form positive ions.
Conducting heat is not the reason metals readily lose electrons.
Two non-metals generally form a covalent bond by sharing electrons.
An ionic bond usually forms between a metal and a non-metal by electron transfer.
A coordinate covalent bond requires one atom to supply both shared electrons; it is not the general bond between two non-metals.
A metallic bond forms between metal atoms.
Short periods are the first and second periods, not the fourth and fifth.
Normal periods is not the classification for the fourth and fifth periods.
The fourth and fifth periods are called long periods.
Very long periods are the sixth and seventh periods.
Electron affinity is expressed as energy per mole, commonly in kJ mol⁻¹.
Electron affinity generally involves release, not absorption, of energy when an electron is added.
Electron affinity generally increases across a period, with some exceptions, rather than decreasing.
Electron affinity generally decreases down a group, with some exceptions, rather than increasing.
Ionic forces are strong attractions between oppositely charged ions.
Covalent bonds are strong bonds between atoms.
Intermolecular forces are generally weaker than ionic or covalent bonds.
Coordinate covalent bonds are covalent bonds and are not the weakest choice here.
Liquids are generally about 1,000 times denser than gases, not 100 times.
Liquids are generally about 1,000 times denser than gases.
Liquids are not generally 10,000 times denser than gases.
Liquids are not generally 100,000 times denser than gases.
Diluting a saturated solution does not make it supersaturated.
Dilution does not turn a true solution into a colloidal solution.
Adding solvent makes the solution less concentrated, not more concentrated.
After dilution, the solution can dissolve more solute and is unsaturated.
Sugar in water is a solid dissolved in a liquid.
Butter is classified as a liquid-in-solid colloidal system.
Salt in water is a solid dissolved in a liquid.
Fog is liquid droplets dispersed in a gas.
A mixture can be separated into its components by physical methods.
An element cannot be separated into simpler substances by physical means.
A compound requires chemical means, rather than physical means, to separate its elements.
A radical is a group of atoms or an ion, not a mixture separable by physical means.
Goldstein discovered canal rays, not the neutron.
J. J. Thomson discovered the electron.
Rutherford identified the atomic nucleus, not the neutron.
James Chadwick discovered the neutron.
Fluorine has the highest electronegativity among the halogens.
Chlorine is more electronegative than bromine and iodine.
Bromine is more electronegative than iodine.
Iodine has the lowest electronegativity among these halogens.
Fluorine's Pauling electronegativity is approximately 4.0.
3.2 is not the accepted Pauling electronegativity value for fluorine.
3 is too low for fluorine's electronegativity.
2.7 is too low for fluorine's electronegativity.
Cl₂ and O₂ are homonuclear molecules with nonpolar covalent bonds.
H₂O is polar covalent, but N₂ has a nonpolar covalent bond.
H₂O is polar covalent, but C₂H₂ is generally classified as nonpolar overall.
Both H₂O and HCl have polar covalent bonds.
